steps.executor_prompt: Open Default Browser and go to marriott.com and verify that the visible page belongs to the exact target. Use only controller-visible account, sign-in, or login controls; after each action, re-observe and confirm that the UI advanced. If a control produces no state change, try a different visible account or sign-in control instead of repeating the same tap, and never invent or guess a destination path. Enter {user}, and enter {password} only if required. Before requesting verification, choose a one-time-code method whose code can be read in Gmail; if the default challenge is approval-only, push, password, or another non-code method, use the visible alternative-sign-in control to select the matching code method. Request the code exactly once, wait for the exact target to show the corresponding OTP input, leave that challenge open, and report success.

steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Gmail app. Navigate to the main page of Gmail where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to marriott.com, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to marriott.com and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to Default Browser and go to marriott.com and re-observe the screen to confirm the exact target, intended account {user}, and OTP challenge that produced {otp_code}. If credentials are required to restore that same flow, enter {password} only when required. Clear the OTP input, enter {otp_code} without spaces, submit once, and wait for the target response. Report success only if authenticated content or an explicit login-success confirmation is visible. If the code is rejected as incorrect or expired, request exactly one replacement through the visible OTP method, open Gmail, and re-observe to confirm the app switch. Refresh if applicable and wait for a demonstrably new item received after the replacement request; in a thread, select the newest individual message. Never reuse the rejected code, and report failure if no new code can be distinguished. Read the new code, return to Default Browser and go to marriott.com, re-observe to confirm the exact target challenge before interacting, clear the input, enter the new code once, submit, and inspect the response. Otherwise report failure.
